prompt: What is the last digit of $2018\times8012$?

solutions.title: Units digits only
solutions.body:
Only the units digits matter: $8\times2=16$, so the last digit is $6$.

**Answer: 6**

prompt: Determine the value of $2^0+1^8$.

solutions.title: Evaluate
solutions.body:
$2^0=1$ and $1^8=1$, so the sum is $2$.

**Answer: 2**

prompt: If $100\div5=4\times A$ then find the value of $A$.

solutions.title: Solve
solutions.body:
$100\div5=20=4\times A$, so $A=5$.

**Answer: 5**

prompt: Determine the value of $x$.

solutions.title: Angles at a point and alternate angles
solutions.body:
The two horizontal lines are parallel. The angle $300^\circ$ is measured round the top vertex, so the angle inside the 'Z' at the top between the transversal and the line going left is $360^\circ-300^\circ=60^\circ$. By alternate angles between the parallel lines, $x=60$.

**Answer: 60**

prompt: $ABCD$ is a square with area $72\text{ cm}^2$. $ABCD$ is split into $9$ identical squares. What is the shaded area in $\text{cm}^2$?

solutions.title: Fraction of the square
solutions.body:
Two of the nine identical squares are shaded: $\frac29\times72=16$.

**Answer: 16**

prompt: The diagram shows kite $ABCD$. What is the size of $\angle ABC$ in degrees?

solutions.title: Symmetry of the kite
solutions.body:
The kite is symmetric about $AC$, so $\angle ABC=\angle ADC$. The angles sum to $360^\circ$: $70^\circ+40^\circ+2\angle ABC=360^\circ$, so $\angle ABC=125^\circ$.

**Answer: 125**

prompt: The solid shown was made by gluing together four identical cubes each with side length $1$ cm. What is the total surface area of the solid in $\text{cm}^2$?

solutions.title: Subtract hidden faces
solutions.body:
Each cube has surface area $6$, so four cubes have $24$. The cubes are joined at $3$ contacts (the solid is connected with no loops), and each contact hides $2$ unit faces: $24-6=18$.

**Answer: 18**

prompt: The sum of four consecutive whole numbers is $2018$. Find the smallest of these numbers.

solutions.title: Mean
solutions.body:
The mean is $2018\div4=504.5$, so the numbers are $503,504,505,506$. The smallest is $503$.

**Answer: 503**

prompt: In the expression $W\times X^Y-Z$, the values of $W$, $X$, $Y$ and $Z$ are $2$, $0$, $1$ and $8$, but not necessarily in that order. What is the maximum possible value of $W\times X^Y-Z$?

solutions.title: Choose the roles
solutions.body:
Subtracting $0$ costs nothing, and putting $0$ anywhere else makes the product tiny ($W\times X^Y$ would be $0$, or at most $8$), so $Z=0$. Now use $1,2,8$: $W=1$ gives $2^8=256$ or $8^2=64$; $W=2$ gives $2\cdot8^1=16$ or $2\cdot1^8=2$; $W=8$ gives $8\cdot2^1=16$ or $8\cdot1^2=8$. The maximum is $256$.

**Answer: 256**

prompt: Sanjeev gets the disease algebritis and must take one green pill and one pink pill each day for three weeks. A green pill costs R1 more than a pink pill. Sanjeev's pills cost R2121 for the three weeks. How many rands does a green pill cost?

solutions.title: Cost per day
solutions.body:
Three weeks is $21$ days, so a green plus a pink pill cost $2121\div21=101$ rand. With the green pill R1 dearer: pink R50, green R51.

**Answer: R51**

prompt: How many $2$-digit odd numbers can be made using the digits $1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8$ if each digit can be used only once in a given number?

solutions.title: Choose last digit first
solutions.body:
The units digit must be odd: $1,3,5$ or $7$ ($4$ choices). The tens digit can be any of the remaining $7$ digits. Total $4\times7=28$.

**Answer: 28**

prompt: The six angles of two different triangles are listed from largest to smallest. The two smallest angles have been left off the list: $120^\circ,80^\circ,65^\circ,37^\circ,\_\_\_,\_\_\_$. In degrees, what is the last angle on the list?

solutions.title: Split the angles
solutions.body:
$120^\circ$ cannot be in a triangle with $80^\circ$ or $65^\circ$ (the sum would exceed $180^\circ$), so $80^\circ$ and $65^\circ$ are in the other triangle, whose third angle is $180-145=35^\circ$. The first triangle contains $120^\circ$, $37^\circ$ and the missing angle $180-157=23^\circ$. The list in order ends $\dots,37,35,23$, so the last angle is $23$.

**Answer: 23**

prompt: The vertices of a $3$-$4$-$5$ right-angled triangle $ABC$ are the centres of three circles that just touch each other. If $AB=3$ cm, $AC=4$ cm and $BC=5$ cm, determine the sum of the diameters of the three circles in cm.

solutions.title: Sides are sums of radii
solutions.body:
Touching circles satisfy $r_A+r_B=3$, $r_A+r_C=4$, $r_B+r_C=5$. Adding: $2(r_A+r_B+r_C)=12$, so the sum of the radii is $6$ and the sum of the diameters is $12$ (the perimeter of the triangle).

**Answer: 12**

prompt: Skylar is sewing together a rectangular quilt. The quilt is $1{,}5$ metres long and $1{,}2$ metres wide, and is made from square pieces of fabric each measuring $15$ cm by $15$ cm. At every point where four squares meet, Skylar plans to sew on a bright button. How many buttons will be needed?

solutions.title: Count the interior points
solutions.body:
The quilt is $150\div15=10$ squares long and $120\div15=8$ squares wide. Points where four squares meet are the interior grid points: $(10-1)\times(8-1)=9\times7=63$.

**Answer: 63**

prompt:
In the sum below, each letter represents a different digit. $ABC$ and $BCC$ are $3$-digit numbers. What is the digit $A$?
$$\begin{array}{cccc}&A&B&C\\+&A&B&C\\\hline&B&C&C\end{array}$$

solutions.title: Column by column
solutions.body:
Units: $C+C$ ends in $C$, so $C=0$. Tens: $B+B$ ends in $C=0$; $B\ne0$, so $B=5$ with a carry of $1$. Hundreds: $A+A+1=B=5$, so $A=2$. Check: $250+250=500$.

**Answer: 2**

prompt: The average of $v$ and $w$ is $200$. The average of $x$, $y$ and $z$ is $150$. Determine the average of $v$, $w$, $x$, $y$ and $z$.

solutions.title: Totals
solutions.body:
$v+w=400$ and $x+y+z=450$. The five numbers total $850$, so the average is $850\div5=170$.

**Answer: 170**

prompt: Some numbers, when divided by $4$, leave a remainder of $3$; when divided by $3$, leave a remainder of $2$; and when divided by $2$, leave a remainder of $1$. Determine the smallest such number.

solutions.title: Add 1
solutions.body:
If $x$ is such a number then $x+1$ is divisible by $4$, $3$ and $2$, i.e. by $12$. The smallest positive such $x$ is $12-1=11$.

**Answer: 11**

prompt: The diagram shown contains $41$ identical squares. Some of the squares have been shaded. What is the least number of squares that still need to be shaded for the diagram to have a line of symmetry?

solutions.title: Try each axis
solutions.body:
The shape has four possible axes of symmetry (vertical, horizontal and the two diagonals). Counting the shaded squares whose mirror images are unshaded, the horizontal axis needs $5$ more squares, the vertical axis needs $4$, one diagonal needs $4$ and the other diagonal needs only $3$. The minimum is $3$.

**Answer: 3**

prompt: Let $\bigstar(x)$ be the sum of the digits of the positive whole number $x$. For example, $\bigstar(8)=8$ and $\bigstar(123)=1+2+3=6$. For how many different $2$-digit numbers $x$ is $\bigstar(\bigstar(x))=3$?

solutions.title: Possible digit sums
solutions.body:
A $2$-digit number has digit sum at most $18$, and $\bigstar(s)=3$ for $s\le18$ means $s=3$ or $s=12$. Digit sum $3$: $12,21,30$ ($3$ numbers). Digit sum $12$: $39,48,57,66,75,84,93$ ($7$ numbers). Total $10$.

**Answer: 10**

prompt: The diagram shows two overlapping circles, $A$ and $B$. The shaded area is $65\text{ m}^2$ while the overlapping area is $15\text{ m}^2$. The ratio of the area of circle $A$ to the area of circle $B$ is $3:2$. By how many $\text{m}^2$ is circle $A$ larger than circle $B$?

solutions.title: Add the areas
solutions.body:
The shaded region is both circles together, so area$(A)$ + area$(B)$ $=65+15=80$ (the overlap is counted twice when adding the two circles). With ratio $3:2$: $A=48$ and $B=32$. The difference is $16$.

**Answer: 16**

prompt: The diagram shows a rectangle inside a semicircle. The rectangle just touches the sides of the semicircle. Two lengths are shown. Determine the area of the rectangle in $\text{cm}^2$.

solutions.title: Pythagoras
solutions.body:
Let the rectangle have length $2x$. The semicircle's radius is $x+1$. The right triangle formed by the centre, the rectangle's lower corner point and its foot has sides $x$, $4$ and hypotenuse $x+1$: $x^2+16=x^2+2x+1$, so $x=7.5$. The rectangle is $15$ by $4$, with area $60$.

**Answer: 60**

prompt: Determine the sum of all integers $x$ which satisfy the equation $(218-x)^{221+x}=1$.

solutions.title: Three cases
solutions.body:
A power equals $1$ when (i) the base is $1$: $218-x=1$, $x=217$; (ii) the exponent is $0$ with non-zero base: $x=-221$ (base $439$); (iii) the base is $-1$ with even exponent: $218-x=-1$, $x=219$, exponent $440$ is even. Sum: $217-221+219=215$.

**Answer: 215**

prompt: Tom was jogging at a constant speed of $10$ km/h along a straight road. Jerry, jogging at a constant speed of $12$ km/h, is $600$ m behind Tom. How many minutes will it take Jerry to catch up with Tom?

solutions.title: Closing speed
solutions.body:
Jerry gains $12-10=2$ km/h on Tom. To close $0.6$ km takes $\frac{0.6}{2}=0.3$ h $=18$ minutes.

**Answer: 18**

prompt: This clock works correctly but the numbers are missing and the clock has been rotated. Use the positions of the hour and minute hands to determine which hour is represented by the letter $A$.

solutions.title: Official reading
solutions.body:
The hour hand is $\frac35$ of the way from one hour marking to the next, so the time is $\frac35\times60=36$ minutes past the hour. The minute hand has therefore just passed the marking for $35$ minutes, which is the number $7$ on a normal clock. The marking $A$ is the next one on, so it represents $8$.

**Answer: 8**

reviewNote: Answer taken from the official key; the picture of the rotated clock could not be fully checked independently.

prompt: A $10\text{ cm}\times6\text{ cm}$ rectangle is divided into five smaller rectangles of $2\text{ cm}\times6\text{ cm}$. Diagonal $AB$ is drawn, as well as a number of smaller diagonals. How much larger, in $\text{cm}^2$, is the shaded area than the unshaded area?

solutions.title: Fractions of the rectangle
solutions.body:
By symmetry and translating pieces, the shaded area is $\frac35$ of the rectangle ($36$ cm$^2$) and the unshaded area is $\frac25$ ($24$ cm$^2$). The difference is $\frac15\times60=12$.

**Answer: 12**
